reason: E1 and E2 show Hf can strengthen and pin boundaries in single-phase HEAs and at high temperature, but none of the cited evidence demonstrates Hf additions to a eutectic HEA, trace-level Hf forming precipitates at interlamellar boundaries, or suppression of room-temperature microcracking. The key premises thus extrapolate from different alloy systems and conditions without direct support.
premises: Hf additions can form precipitates that strengthen alloys without severely reducing ductility
Hf-rich phases can pin grain/phase boundaries and suppress boundary sliding at high temperature
The cited Hf effects apply to eutectic HEAs with lamellar FCC/B2 microstructures
Trace Hf (<1 at.%) will form nanoscale precipitates specifically at interlamellar boundaries
Pinning interlamellar boundaries will suppress room-temperature microcrack initiation and improve ductility
